scenes.narration: How did DeepSeek-R1 achieve OpenAI o1-level reasoning without giant training budgets? The answer is GRPO, or Group Relative Policy Optimization.

props.title: How DeepSeek-R1 Thinks: GRPO
props.subtitle: Supercharging AI reasoning without massive critic models

scenes.narration: Traditional reinforcement learning like PPO requires training a massive critic model alongside the policy. GRPO eliminates the critic entirely by sampling a group of answers for each prompt.
By removing the need for a separate value network, GRPO cuts training memory in half and lets models discover emergent self-reflection and chain-of-thought autonomously.

props.title: PPO vs DeepSeek GRPO
leftPoints: Hard to balance policy and value loss
rightPoints: No Critic network needed (0 extra params)
Normalizes rewards directly within the group
Cuts reinforcement learning VRAM in half

scenes.narration: The advantage for each response is simply its reward minus the group mean, divided by the group standard deviation. The best reasoning paths get reinforced, and bad paths get penalized.

props.title: Group Relative Advantage
props.explanation: Calculates relative advantage purely within sampled group G without requiring a value function network.

scenes.narration: GRPO proves you don't need closed-source black boxes to train world-class reasoning models. Pure reinforcement learning is the new frontier.
